images.caption: With a steep hill at its outer edge, a gravel-paved pathway clings to the south wall of the Glyndor Mansion, as seen on a June 2022 visit to the Wave Hill Public Garden. One of two historic homes located within this expertly manicured 28-acre expanse, Glyndor is a sprawling Colonial Revival-style beauty designed by the firm of Butler & Corse and built in 1927 on the foundation of an earlier home that was lost to fire. The property's original owner was George Walbridge Perkins (1862-1920), a towering figure in local financial spheres who occupied executive posts in the New York Life Insurance Company and with J. P. Morgan. His widow Evelina - at the suggestion of Robert Moses, who was then serving as commissioner of the New York City Parks Department and chairman of the New York State Council of Parks - donated the property to the city upon her death in 1960, and along with the grounds of the adjacent Wave Hill House, it was opened to visitors five years later as a public garden and arboretum. Glyndor in particular is now used as an art gallery.

images.filename: Wave Hill - 20220616 - 21 - pergola at Great Lawn.jpg
images.caption: The pergola that rims the west edge of the Great Lawn at Wave Hill Public Garden in the Bronx not only offers superlative views of the Palisades and the Hudson River, but is a pleasant sight in itself, styled with a profusion of intricately arranged seasonal potted plants into an ambience redolent of a tropical oasis. As seen during a June 2022 visit.

images.filename: Wave Hill - 20220616 - 24 - Perkins Visitor Center & Gift Shop (interior).jpg
images.caption: The interior of the Perkins Visitor Center at Wave Hill Public Garden in the Bronx, as seen during a June 2022 visit. Once a garage and carriage house for the adjacent Glyndor Mansion, it's been redesigned and repurposed for modern-day purposes and, as can be seen here, is principally used as the Wave Hill gift shop.
